label: tfim_6

card.name: gaussian_majorana_global_resynthesis
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs rotations; measurement_free; 2 <= qubits <= 8; and the op list must be fermionic-Gaussian as a whole, i.e. v4.api.fermion.is_gaussian(ops) is true: every Clifford in it maps Majorana monomials g_a -> +-g_b (h, s, sdg, z, x, cx/cz in the JW-local pattern) and every rotation's front-frame Pauli (v4.api.pauli.frames) is a Majorana BILINEAR, bilinear_of(P, n) != None. Circuits with any rotation whose Pauli is a weight-4-or-higher non-bilinear monomial are excluded and cost nothing. On tfim_6 the fingerprint already reports free_fermion = true, majorana_planes = 12, generator_algebra_rank = 22.
card.identity: A Gaussian circuit on n qubits is, in the 2n Majorana operators g_1..g_2n, a single element R of O(2n): U g_a U^dag = sum_b R_{ba} g_b. Compose the whole op list ONCE into that R (orthogonal_of(ops)), then re-emit U from R instead of from its 160 gates: Givens-factor R into at most 2n(2n-1)/2 = 66 adjacent-plane rotations G(a, a+1, theta_i) times a residual sign diagonal (givens(R)), and emit each plane rotation as the one-parameter Gaussian gate exp(theta_i g_a g_{a+1} / 2) = plane_rotation(a, a+1, theta_i, n) -- a single Rz conjugated by a fixed Clifford (JW string), one non-Clifford rotation each. The residual sign diagonal is a product of Z/S gates: pure Clifford, free. Plane rotations whose theta is a multiple of pi/4 (on_grid) are emitted as Clifford/T and cost nothing extra. Drop them from the Rz tally. The output op list replaces the entire circuit (the rule is one global match, not a window): trigger returns the single match {whole circuit} when the precondition holds and the emitted rotation count is strictly below the current one.
card.correctness: Gaussian (matchgate / free-fermion) unitaries form a group: a product of exponentials of Majorana bilinears is the exponential of a bilinear, and the adjoint action on the 2n-dimensional real Majorana span is a faithful homomorphism onto SO(2n) (O(2n) once the parity/sign diagonal is included), with kernel exactly the global phase. Therefore R determines U up to global phase, which is unobservable (invariant 6) and which the judge's phase-aligned distance already quotients out. Givens' theorem factors any R in O(2n) exactly into adjacent plane rotations times a sign diagonal; each plane rotation lifts back to exp(theta g_a g_{a+1} / 2) by the same homomorphism. So the re-emitted op list equals the original up to phase: the identity is exact, not a fit, and the angles are read off R by arctan2, not optimised. The only error is float round-off in forming R (~1e-14, orders below any ledger charge); the judge's phase-aligned operator distance on the whole-circuit check confirms it, and the rule declines (returns no match) if that distance exceeds 1e-12 rather than drawing from the budget. Ancilla-free, measurement-free, so the specification contract is the unitary one.
card.trigger: One match per circuit. Fires when: (1) every op is in {h, s, sdg, x, z, cx, cz, rz, t, tdg} with no measurement; (2) frames(ops) gives, for every rotation record, a Pauli P with bilinear_of(P, n) != None; (3) orthogonal_of(ops) returns an R with R^T R = I to 1e-10; (4) len(givens(R) rotations with not on_grid(theta)) < number of current non-Clifford rotations. On tfim_6: 160 off-grid Rz in, at most 66 (expected 22-66, since generator_algebra_rank = 22 bounds the plane-rotation support actually used) out.
card.expected_effect: The 160 off-grid Rz collapse to the at most 66 Givens plane rotations of the single O(12) element (22 if the rank-22 generator algebra means R lives in a 22-dimensional subgroup, which the fingerprint's generator_algebra_rank = 22 against 66 for full O(12) suggests). The 180 cx / 192 h / 102 sdg / 29 s / 12 z Clifford skeleton is replaced by the JW conjugation strings of the emitted plane rotations plus one sign diagonal, which also cuts CNOT count (tie-break 3). The T saving is double: fewer rotations to synthesize, AND each surviving rotation gets a larger eps_rz = (eps/2)/N_Rz because N_Rz fell, so gridsynth pays ~3*log2(160/N_Rz) fewer T on each one. At N_Rz = 66: 66 * ~50 T = ~3300 T total, versus 8560 now. At N_Rz = 22: ~1370 T.
card.source: Terhal & DiVincenzo, 'Classical simulation of noninteracting-fermion quantum circuits', PRA 65 032325 (2002); Jozsa & Miyake, 'Matchgates and classical simulation of quantum circuits', Proc. R. Soc. A 464 (2008); Givens/Thouless decomposition of O(2n) as in Kivlichan et al., 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120 110501 (2018)
card.notes: This is lever (c) on the one circuit where levers (a) and (b) have exactly zero headroom: pyzx/TKET/BQSKit all sit at 8560 and DPF is worse (9600) because snapping 160 individually-cheap angles buys nothing. None of them represent the circuit as a group element, so none can see that 160 rotations parameterise an object with at most 66 parameters. The floor's Pauli-frame merging is local axis matching and cannot do this: the merged axes here are 22 distinct bilinear classes with 160 parity classes, all already fully folded (foldable_remaining = 0).

harness: lowers the primary metric on tfim_6@0.001: 8560 -> 3354

label: hhl_8

card.name: commuting_pauli_cluster_diagonalization
card.precondition: family dv_angle (Clifford+Rz op list, no Toffoli/CCZ, measurement-free); needs `rotations` and `nonclifford_rz`; 2 <= n_qubits <= 14 (so `v4.api.sim.unitary` can certify a cluster window). Requires at least 2 rotations whose front-frame Pauli axes coincide, i.e. len(frames(ops)) > number of distinct axis keys. On hhl_8: 475 rotations over 142 axis classes, so it triggers.
card.identity: Write the circuit, via `v4.api.pauli.frames`, as an ordered product of signed Pauli exponentials times a residual Clifford: C = W * prod_j exp(-i theta_j P_j / 2). Partition the ORDERED list P_1..P_m greedily into consecutive maximal clusters S_1,...,S_r such that the Paulis inside each cluster pairwise commute. Inside a cluster all factors commute, so they may be permuted freely and every pair with the same axis key merges (theta_i + s*theta_j, one rotation deleted, s = relative sign). Then, for each cluster, find a Clifford U_t that SIMULTANEOUSLY diagonalizes all of its Paulis: the cluster's Paulis span an isotropic (self-commuting) subspace of the symplectic space, so Gaussian elimination over GF(2) on the (x|z) tableau gives U_t built from H, S and CX with U_t P U_t^dag = +-Z_{m} for every member. Each exponential becomes a diagonal CNOT+Rz phase-polynomial term with affine parity label `labels()`; equal labels in the cluster merge again (`v4.api.phasepoly.equal_label_pairs`), and the resulting diagonal block is re-emitted as a parity-network CNOT ladder carrying one Rz per DISTINCT label. The cluster is emitted as U_t^dag (diagonal block) U_t; U_t^dag U_{t+1} is fused as a single Clifford between consecutive clusters and the trailing W is appended, so no Clifford cost is duplicated.
card.correctness: (1) `frames` is an exact rewriting: conjugating a Z-rotation through a Clifford prefix gives exp(-i theta (C^dag P C)/2), so the ordered exponential product times the residual Clifford equals the original circuit up to global phase. (2) If [P_i, P_j] = 0 then exp(-i a P_i/2) and exp(-i b P_j/2) commute exactly, so permutation within a cluster is an identity; and exp(-i a P/2) exp(-i b (sP)/2) = exp(-i (a + s b) P/2) since P^2 = I, which is the merge. (3) A set of pairwise-commuting Paulis generates an abelian subgroup, i.e. an isotropic subspace under the symplectic form; the Clifford group acts transitively on isotropic subspaces, so a Clifford U_t with U_t P U_t^dag in {+-Z-type} for all members exists and is produced constructively by symplectic Gaussian elimination. (4) Diagonal exponentials of Z-type Paulis are phase-polynomial terms; two terms with equal affine parity label are the same function of the computational basis state and add, and `v4.api.phasepoly.witness` proves the re-emitted parity network equals the diagonal block in O(ops) with no matrices. Every step is exact up to global phase; the frozen judge re-checks each cluster window with exact D[omega] when both sides are Clifford+T and phase-aligned operator distance otherwise.
card.trigger: Compute R = frames(ops). Walk R in order building consecutive maximal pairwise-commuting clusters (a record joins the open cluster iff its Pauli commutes with every Pauli already in it, else it opens a new cluster). Emit one match per cluster that (a) contains at least two records sharing an axis key, OR (b) contains at least two records whose labels coincide after diagonalization, i.e. the cluster's distinct-label count is strictly less than its record count. Clusters with no collapse are not matched, so they cost nothing. Each match carries the cluster's record positions, so `apply` rewrites exactly the op range it owns.
card.expected_effect: Deletes off-grid Rz gates: hhl_8 has 475 non-Clifford rotations but only 142 distinct front-frame Pauli axis classes, and the floor's merge rules could only fire when the later Pauli commuted with EVERY intervening rotation Pauli - a sequential condition that fails here (foldable_remaining = 0 while 333 same-axis duplicates survive). Clustering replaces that sequential test with a cluster-local one: within a commuting cluster the order is free, so same-axis duplicates merge even though they do not commute with rotations outside the cluster, and simultaneous diagonalization collapses a second group of rotations whose front-frame axes differ but whose diagonal parity labels coincide. Each deleted off-grid rotation removes one gridsynth call, currently ~59 T at eps_rz = 2.1e-6, and shrinking N_Rz also raises eps_rz for the survivors, making each remaining rotation slightly cheaper. The added Clifford cost (U_t, U_t^dag, parity ladders) is CNOT/H/S only and is free in T; cost order is lexicographic with T first, so it is paid in the third key only. I expect roughly a third of the 333 same-axis duplicates to land inside a single commuting cluster (hhl_8's rotations come from controlled-e^{iAt} Trotter blocks whose Pauli terms are largely mutually commuting within a block) plus a smaller label-collapse contribution: ~100-110 rotations removed.
card.source: E. van den Berg and K. Temme, 'Circuit optimization of Hamiltonian simulation by simultaneous diagonalization of Pauli clusters', Quantum 4, 322 (2020); simultaneous-diagonalization construction as in Aaronson-Gottesman (symplectic Gaussian elimination) and parity-network emission as in Amy, Azimzadeh, Mosca, 'On the controlled-NOT complexity of controlled-NOT-phase circuits' (2018).
